Rice to Water Ratio Calculator

On the stovetop, use 1½ cups of water for 1 cup of white rice and simmer 15 to 18 minutes. Brown rice takes 2½ cups and 40 to 45 minutes. In an Instant Pot, use 1 cup of water per cup of rice.

Rice to water ratios

Stovetop, by volume: cups of water for 1 cup of dry rice
RiceRice : waterSimmerRinse
White long-grain1 : 1.515 to 18 minutes
Jasmine1 : 1.515 minutesRinse first
Basmati1 : 1.515 minutesRinse first

Instant Pot: 1 cup of water per cup of white or brown rice, from the Instant Pot manual’s grain-to-water table. White rice cooks 4 minutes and brown rice 22 minutes at high pressure, then 10 minutes natural release.

How it works

The calculator multiplies your dry rice by the ratio for that rice and cooker. On the stovetop: bring the water to a boil, add the rice, cover, and simmer on low for the time shown. Then take it off the heat and let it rest 10 minutes with the lid on before you fluff it. It all runs in your browser. Nothing you type is sent anywhere or saved.

A rice cooker uses about the same ratio as the stovetop. Measure with a regular US cup, not the small cup that comes with the cooker, which holds 180 ml. An Instant Pot uses less water because almost nothing boils off with the lid locked.

Ways to use it

  • Weeknight white rice. 1 cup dry makes about 3 cups cooked.
  • Brown rice meal prep. Cook a big pot, cool it fast, and refrigerate.
  • Sushi rice. Rinse well and use less water so it stays sticky but firm.
  • Rice cooker vs stovetop. Same ratio, different measuring cup.

Questions

Should I rinse the rice?

For jasmine, basmati and sushi rice, yes: rinse in cold water until it runs mostly clear. It washes off loose starch, so the grains don’t clump. Plain long-grain white rice is fine either way.

Why does brown rice take longer?

Brown rice still has its bran layer, which water has to soak through. It needs more water and about 40 to 45 minutes, against 15 to 18 for white rice.

Can I use the same ratio in a rice cooker?

Yes, measured with a regular US cup. Or measure with the cooker’s own cup and fill to the matching line in the bowl. Just don’t mix the two cups.

What if I lift the lid?

Try not to. Lifting the lid lets the steam out, and the steam is doing the cooking. Wait until the time is up, then let it rest covered for 10 minutes.

Is anything saved?

No. The calculator runs in your browser and nothing is saved or sent anywhere.
